input: Write a due diligence memo on Revolut

output.company: Revolut (Revolut Group Holdings Ltd; key UK operating entity Revolut Ltd)

business.claim: Company claim: Revolut describes a technology-driven, diversified financial-services platform serving retail customers and businesses with spending, saving, investing, international transfers, payments, lending, crypto and subscription products.

Company claim: its major 2025 revenue engines included subscriptions, card payments, wealth, FX, savings/money-market funds, investments, crypto, lending, payments and Revolut Business; 11 product lines each exceeded approximately £100m of annual revenue.

Company claim: Revolut serves 80+ million personal customers and 800K+ business customers globally, supports 160+ countries and regions, and operates as a bank in 30+ countries; the FY2025 release specified 68.3m retail and 767K business customers at year-end.

Company claim: 2025 product expansion included ATMs beginning in Spain, mobile plans in the UK and Poland, eSIM connectivity, mortgage refinancing in Lithuania, Kids & Teens, Revolut Pay and RevPoints; availability depends on customer residence.

Reuters reports that Revolut has no physical bank branches and monetizes a diversified product mix rather than relying solely on lending; Reuters analysis also describes subscriptions, fees, interest income and crypto as important revenue sources.

traction.claim: Company claim: retail customers grew 30% to 68.3m during 2025, business customers grew 33% to 767K, total customer balances grew 66% to $67.5bn, and total transaction volume grew 65% to $1.7tn.

Company claim: Revolut Business processed $365bn (£277bn) of 2025 transaction volume, and Revolut Business represented 16% of total income; expansion-market business volume grew more than 140% year on year in Singapore, Australia and the US.
Company claim: more than 750,000 companies used Revolut Business in 2025, with about 30,000 joining each month, including Booking.com.

Company claim: Booking.com adopted Revolut Pay for one-click checkout and Revolut Business for day-to-day operations; Revolut said almost 2m customers were monthly active Revolut Pay users and about 9m users had purchased on Booking.com.
Company claim: over 63% of new retail customers in 2025 joined through word-of-mouth or referrals, and RevPoints reached 17m users across 36 markets, up from 6.6m at year-end 2024.
Company claim: Revolut announced a multi-year strategic partnership with Google Cloud for infrastructure, AI/machine learning and fraud detection.

team.claim: The company identifies Nik Storonsky as Co-founder and CEO; its biography says he previously traded emerging-market equity derivatives at Credit Suisse and Lehman Brothers.
The company identifies Vlad Yatsenko as Co-founder and Non-Executive Board Member; his biography describes prior financial-software engineering work at UBS and Deutsche Bank.
The company lists Martin Gilbert as Chair and Victor Stinga as CFO; Gilbert previously co-founded Aberdeen Asset Management and held senior roles at Standard Life, Sky and FirstGroup.

On 1 July 2026, Vlad Yatsenko left the CTO role and became a non-executive director; Donato Lucia, previously head of technology, replaced him as Vice President of Technology. Revolut gave no reason for the change.
The company says Donato Lucia oversees a global engineering organization of more than 1,400 employees and previously held engineering positions at lastminute.com, IBM and HP.

funding.claim: Fireround's structured funding record reports a $2.3m 2015 funding round led by Balderton, a £6.75m Series A in 2016 led by Balderton, and a $66m Series B in 2017 led by Index Ventures; aggregator data.
Company claim: Revolut raised $250m in a 2018 Series C led by DST Global Partners at a $1.7bn valuation.
Company claim: Revolut raised $500m in Series D funding in February 2020 at a $5.5bn valuation, followed by an $80m extension in July 2020 led by TSG Consumer Partners.
Company claim: Revolut raised $800m in Series E in July 2021, led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Tiger Global, at a $33bn valuation.

Reuters reported that a 2024 secondary share sale valued Revolut at $45bn and was led by Coatue and D1 Capital Partners with existing investor Tiger Global; this was a secondary sale rather than stated new primary capital.

Company claim: a November 2025 share sale established a $75bn valuation, was led by Coatue, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Fidelity Management & Research Company, and included NVentures, a16z, Franklin Templeton and T. Rowe Price; the company did not disclose transaction size in the opened release.

Reuters reported that a July 2026 secondary share sale was underway at $2,017 per share, implying a $115bn valuation; media reports said Revolut was targeting at least $750m of shares. This is the latest valuation located, not confirmed primary fundraising.

financial_signals.claim: Company-reported FY2025 revenue was £4.5bn ($6.0bn), up 46%; profit before tax was £1.7bn ($2.3bn), up 57%, with a 38% PBT margin; net profit was £1.3bn ($1.7bn), the fifth consecutive profitable year.
Company-reported FY2024 revenue was £3.1bn, up 72%; PBT was £1.1bn, up 149%; net profit was £790m.

Company claim: the lending portfolio grew 120% year on year to £2.2bn ($2.9bn) in 2025, while interest income rose 23% to £974m ($1.3bn); 90% of assets were held in cash, cash equivalents and Treasury Investments.

Official annual-report data show average Group headcount increased from 9,932 in 2024 to 10,909 in 2025; the company describes this as 10% year-on-year average-headcount growth and reports a £10bn five-year investment plan including new roles.

Reuters analysis says Revolut's revenue per customer remains a fraction of established banks' and its loan-to-deposit ratio was about 6% at end-2025, versus 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale; Reuters identifies scaling lending as a future risk and opportunity.

No verified group-wide layoffs figure was found in the opened official reports or reputable press sources for 2024-11-03 through 2026-11-03; the opened company reports instead show headcount growth and hiring plans.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: The FCA Register shows Revolut Ltd (FRN 900562, company no. 08804411) as a registered authorised electronic-money institution with payment and e-money permissions; the record also shows an active clone warning for 'Al-pha Bank (Clone of FCA Authorised Firm)' added 17 May 2023.

Italy's Competition Authority fined Revolut Securities Europe UAB and Revolut Group Holdings Ltd €5m over misleading disclosures on fractional-share investments; it separately fined Revolut Group Holdings Ltd and Revolut Bank UAB €5m over aggressive/insufficiently explained account suspensions and €1.5m over unclear Italian-IBAN information. The decision concerns named group entities, not Revolut Ltd.

Reuters reported that Lithuania's central bank fined Revolut €3.5m after finding violations and shortcomings in monitoring business relationships and transactions; the regulated entities were Revolut Bank UAB/Revolut Holdings Europe, not UK Revolut Ltd.

The Bank of Lithuania previously found AML/CTF deficiencies at Revolut Bank UAB and Revolut Payments UAB involving onboarding risk factors, higher-risk/PEP approvals and collection of relationship-purpose information; it issued warnings and imposed €50,000 and €150,000 penalties, respectively, with remediation required by 30 June 2022.

Reuters reported that Revolut confirmed a September 2026 data incident in which fraudulent requests from a legitimate government-agency email domain led to disclosure of sensitive customer data; later reporting put the affected population at about 680 customers, while Revolut said its core systems and customer funds were unaffected.

In Uzbekov v Revolut [2024] EWHC 98 (KB), the High Court struck out an ex-customer's account-closure claim as an abuse of process; the legal analysis says Revolut had blocked and closed accounts after an AML alert/adverse media and filed a suspicious-activity report. The source does not identify the legal entity as Revolut Ltd.

reputation.claim: As displayed on 3 November 2026, Glassdoor showed 4.3/5 from 6,583 reviews, 84% would recommend, and 94% CEO approval; its AI summary described a fast, high-standard culture but recurring comments about pressure, long hours/weekends, shifting priorities and inconsistent management. Aggregator data and anonymous reviews.

As displayed on 3 November 2026, Trustpilot showed 4.7/5 from 483,200 reviews; its AI summary was overwhelmingly positive but also identified complaints about outages temporarily blocking access to funds and causing travel inconvenience. Trustpilot says it does not fact-check specific claims.

Reuters reported that Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in 2024 and 2025 for fraud cases in which customers were tricked into sending money to scammers, based on Ombudsman data compiled by Which?; this is a reported complaint signal, not a finding of misconduct by the company.

The Guardian reported former staff criticism of aggressive targets, unpaid work, severe pressure and high turnover; Revolut denied that its culture initiative was directly intended to appease the FCA, while a senior people executive acknowledged that the culture had previously seemed more aggressive.

red_flags.claim: Regulatory/compliance risk: the group has faced a €3.5m Lithuanian AML fine and an €11.5m Italian competition/consumer-protection decision involving account restrictions, investment disclosures and IBAN information; entity scope must be separated carefully in diligence.

Operational/data risk: in 2026 a social-engineering incident led to disclosure of sensitive data for about 680 customers, although Reuters reported that core infrastructure and customer funds were unaffected.

Customer-conduct risk: Reuters reports Revolut was Britain's most-complained-about bank for APP-fraud cases in 2024 and 2025, while the Italian regulator separately found aggressive and insufficiently explained account restrictions.

Valuation/liquidity risk: the latest $115bn price was reported for a secondary employee/investor share sale, not disclosed primary capital; Reuters said the company was targeting at least $750m of shares and that the company had not yet provided final sale details.
Key-person/leadership risk: co-founder Vlad Yatsenko stepped down from CTO in July 2026, with no reason disclosed, although he remained on the board and Donato Lucia assumed technology leadership.

output.verdict: Revolut presents a strong first-pass profile: rapid customer and transaction growth, substantial FY2025 revenue and profitability, broad product diversification, and continued international licensing momentum. The investment case needs closer work on entity-by-entity regulatory exposure, AML/customer-access controls, the 2026 data incident, the durability of revenue per customer as lending scales, and whether the reported $115bn secondary valuation is supported by a completed transaction and primary-capital needs.
missing_fields: Complete current C-suite roster and dated executive history beyond the leadership facts verified above
Complete court-docket and litigation search across all Revolut group entities
Final outcome and appeal status of the Italian Competition Authority decision
Exact size and final completion details of the July 2026 $115bn secondary share sale
Independent verification of customer counts, revenue and profit beyond company-reported figures
Verified group-wide layoffs figure for the two years ending 2026-11-03
Independent sanctions-screening result for the company, subsidiaries, directors and material counterparties
